verdict: The Jakarta Running Festival is Indonesia's answer to the multi-day running festival model: four days (22-25 October 2026) and four distances (42K, 21K, 10K, 5K) spread across a long weekend in the capital [1]. A full marathon in Jakarta itself is a genuinely rare proposition, since most of Indonesia's marquee marathons run in Bali, Jogja, or Borobudur rather than the capital [1][2]. Registration is open in the late-bird tier, but the exact venue within Jakarta hasn't been published yet, so treat this as a promising but still-firming-up listing rather than a fully locked-in race [1][2]. For runners who specifically want a major marathon inside Jakarta with festival energy, it's worth watching closely as venue and course details land.

sections.heading: Four Days, Four Distances in the Capital
paragraphs: The Jakarta Running Festival 2026 spans four days, October 22-25, and offers four distances -- a full marathon (42.195km), half marathon (21.1km), 10K, and 5K [1]. Spreading the field across four separate race days is the multi-day festival model rather than a single crowded start line, which typically means smaller waves per distance and less congestion at any one gun time.

That format also gives runners flexibility: someone traveling to Jakarta for the marathon could plausibly cheer on a friend running the 5K or 10K on a different day of the same long weekend, which is part of what makes multi-day festivals popular as travel-and-race trips.

sections.heading: A Rare Full Marathon in Jakarta Itself
paragraphs: What makes this event stand out on Indonesia's race calendar isn't the format -- it's the location. The country's best-known marathons, from Borobudur to events in Bali and Jogja, are set in scenic or heritage locations outside the capital [2]. A certified full marathon staged in Jakarta proper is comparatively unusual, giving runners based in or traveling to the capital a marathon option without a separate trip to another province.

October also puts the race at the edge of Jakarta's wet season, so mornings are typically warm and humid with a real chance of rain during the event window -- worth factoring into gear and pacing plans regardless of which distance you run.
